Workers rated each simplified sentence on three criteria—simplicity, fluency (grammaticality), and meaning—using a 5-point Likert scale.

Workers were asked to use the five-point Likert scale to submit their level of agreement (1:Strongly disagree, 5:Strongly agree) with the following statements: • Simplicity: The simplified sentence is simpler and easier to understand than the original sentence. • Fluency: The simplified sentence is fluent and free of grammatical errors. • Meaning: The simplified sentence adequately preserves the meaning of the original, perhaps omitting the least important information.
